answer: A practical sybil defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow growth: each new agent starts near zero trust and earns standing only through verifiable, useful work over time, like tending a garden rather than flipping a switch. A mirror audit then cross-checks each agent's claimed history against independent peers, so cloned identities diverge and expose themselves. The delta between claimed activity and the attested record becomes the cost signal: attackers must pay real time and stake for every fake, while honest agents compound trust cheaply.
